title: Private: KMS envelope rotation caused RBAC binding drift and missing audit events — urgent patch
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: A subset of Private customers reported that after an automated KMS envelope key rotation their service integrations (SSO/RBAC role bindings and audit pipelines) intermittently failed to authorize requests or did not emit audit events for admin role changes.
Impact: customers running Private control plane (VPC) experienced 5–30 min windows of authorization errors (403) for service-to-service calls and a truncation of audit-stream events for role/grant updates. Multiple high-touch customers escalated to SE/CS within two hours.
Hypothesis / Root cause: the envelope rotation produced a transient key alias flip that allowed signed SAML assertions and token envelope unwraps to succeed for stale keys but dropped some signed audit events at the audit-forwarder layer due to an unhandled KeyError when decrypting older envelope metadata. This in turn caused RBAC binding reconciliation jobs to skip writes when audit confirmations were missing, producing binding drift.
Reproduction steps: 1) Trigger KMS envelope rotation on a Private control plane cluster with active SCIM/SAML connectors. 2) Execute a service token refresh using envelope-wrapped KEK. 3) Observe 403s in auth-proxy logs and gaps in audit-forwarder topic (kafka/audit-events).
Observed evidence: - Auth-proxy logs (see dashboard) show signature verification paths falling back then raising DecryptionFailure in 21% of rotated envelopes. - Audit-forwarder logs show an uncaught KeyError followed by silent drop: "KeyError: envelope_metadata["version"]" - Customer stacktraces and timed traces uploaded to S3: s3://private-incident-uploads/2025-02-28/ENG-20678/
Timeline: rotation initiated 2025-02-28T03:12Z; first customer error reports 03:17Z; on-call triage 03:22Z; mitigation applied 04:05Z (manual alias pin); full customer recovery by 04:20Z.
Immediate mitigations implemented: - Manual alias pin to previous KEK for affected clusters (rollback) - Temporary increased telemetry on envelope unwrap paths and audit-forwarder errors - Hourly stakeholder sync with SEs for impacted customers
Scope & priority: Affects Private clusters that have recent automated envelope rotations and use SAML/SCIM connectors and audit-forwarder to external logging. High risk for compliance customers because of missing audit trails.
Proposed fix: 1) Hotpatch: Add defensively-handled envelope_metadata parsing in audit-forwarder to tolerate missing fields and queue events to retry rather than drop. 2) Hotpatch: Make envelope unwrap logic in auth-proxy tolerate dual-key verification during a 5-minute rotation window (try new alias, then fallback to last-known KEK without throwing unrecoverable errors). 3) Postmortem/long-term: Harden rotation orchestration to publish a rotation-ready marker and add reconciliation for RBAC binding jobs to re-query the audit stream if confirmations are missing.
Rollout plan: - Patch branch: PR #https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/pull/3489 - Canary on 2 lowest-risk affected clusters for 30m (monitor auth-proxy and audit throughput) - Expand to remaining impacted private clusters over 6 hours if canary shows <1% error rate.
QA & Validation: - Integration test that simulates overlapping key aliases and ensures audit-forwarder retries. - Stress test with synthetic rotations on staging with SAML connector.
Owners & reviewers: - Primary owner: Diego Ramirez - On-call support: Lara Nguyen - Security review: Priya Nair - PM communicator: Oliver Grant
